source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's HOU3-HOU4 campus in Houston publishes 84 MW of IT capacity, the largest figure of any Texas facility mapped here, and the only number that speaks to AI scale.

The campus pairs that load with 347,000 square feet of technical space, about 242 square feet per megawatt. That is a floorplan fact, not a compute fact. It says nothing about what silicon goes inside, and the operator publishes no rack density. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 84 MW is roughly 2,100 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a traditional enterprise density, it is roughly 8,400. The gap between those two numbers decides whether this campus matters to AI, and the spec page cannot resolve it.

Texas is the deepest market mapped here, with 137 facilities, but only 19 publish a megawatt figure at all. Those 19 total 475.41 MW, so this one campus is 17.7 percent of all published Texas capacity. That share is a statement about disclosure as much as construction. Most of the state's mapped footprint is invisible in capacity terms, so one operator willing to publish a number can top a ranking without that ranking meaning what it appears to mean.

What the data does not cover: no tenant, no accelerator count, no power procurement, no interconnection status, and no announced expansion. The single certification, Green Globes, is a whole-building environmental rating that qualifies the campus for general commercial occupancy, not for any specific workload.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
